/speckit-specify This repository already contains `logredact`, a command-line tool that removes personal data from log files. Read the existing code and any documentation in the repository before changing it. Change it as follows; everything else it does now must keep working exactly as it does.

1. **Phone numbers.** Phone numbers in international format, a `+` followed by 8 to 15 digits such as `+14155552671`, become `[PHONE]`. With `--count`, the summary on standard error becomes `emails=N ips=N cards=N phones=N`.

2. **Output folder.** A new option `--out-dir DIR` writes the redacted lines of each FILE to a file with the same name in DIR (the file's name only, without its directories) instead of to standard output. DIR is created, with any missing parent directories, if it does not exist, and an existing file of that name in DIR is replaced. When every FILE has been processed, the tool prints `wrote N files` to standard output, where N is the number of output files written. A FILE that cannot be read is handled as it is now: an error message naming the file on standard error, and exit status 2.

Examples, for files `app.log` (containing `user jane@example.com`) and `web.log` (containing `GET / from 10.0.0.7`):

```
$ printf 'call +14155552671 now\n' | python -m logredact
call [PHONE] now

$ printf 'a@b.io +442071838750\n' | python -m logredact --count
[EMAIL] [PHONE]
emails=1 ips=0 cards=0 phones=1        <- on standard error

$ python -m logredact --out-dir clean app.log web.log
wrote 2 files
```

### What I read first

`src/logredact/{cli,redact,__main__}.py`, the feature-001 spec and `contracts/cli.md`, and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. The spec has a "Relationship to feature 001" table marking each existing requirement as unchanged, extended, or superseded, so the "everything else must keep working" instruction is binding as FR-005/FR-017 and measurable as SC-003.

### Three judgement calls worth your attention

1. **Phone gets the *lowest* precedence (rank 4, after card).** The rules overlap for a `+` plus 13–15 Luhn-valid digits. I confirmed against the running code that `+4222222222222` is redacted today as `+[CARD]`; ranking phone last keeps it that way. Ranking phone higher would silently reclassify such spans and break your compatibility instruction. Every "unchanged" claim in the Edge Cases was verified by running the current `redact_line`, not assumed.

2. **`--out-dir` with no FILE is a usage error (exit 2).** Your description defines the option entirely in terms of "each FILE", and stdin has no name to derive one from. Falling back to stdout or to a file named `<stdin>` would both be the constitution's forbidden "substitute a reasonable value".

3. **I added three requirements your description doesn't mention, because writing to disk is new surface.** Without them the feature would ship real defects: a FILE of `../../etc/passwd` must only ever produce `DIR/passwd` (SR-005); a symlink planted at an output path must not be written through (SR-006); and `--out-dir .` must not truncate the input file it is reading (SR-008). The constitution's path-containment and file-permission controls also forced `0o700` directories / `0o600` files.

Also specified but unstated by you: `wrote 1 file` is singular, and N counts FILE arguments processed (so `logs/a/app.log logs/b/app.log` reports 2 while leaving one file).
